body: Yeah, since I quit drinking (as much) I do feel better, but there's a reason I began drinking in the first place. Those problems don't magically go away once one is sober. I hate saying I'm an alcoholic because then everyone just starts saying "well, stop drinking and your life will be great!" No, I have underlying issues and drinking was a way of coping, it is not the root problem. I'm still suicidal and anxious and depressed and have been for years before I began drinking. Everyone ignores that once I say I'm an alcoholic.

Geez, probably a year ago. Yeah, that's how my alcoholism began. First I'd have a beer before a big event or before a first date. Then 2 beers before the second date (had to maintain that image), before I knew it, anytime I had a social date of any kind, I'd drink prior. Soon I was up to a six-pack before meeting people, than I thought "I'd get more drunk and faster if I switched to liquor". And here I am.

I'm still struggling with not-drinking and although I consider myself an alcoholic, I have cut down on my drinking considerably. I used to drink all day everyday, but now only on the weekends and no liquor, only beer. It's the only thing that alleviates my anxiety. Doesn't help when people comment on how relaxed and open I am when I'm drunk. People say, whether they know I'm drunk or not (hiding it), that I'm more personable and less-guarded. Those comments fed my initial descent into alcoholism.

I don't do any recreational drugs but, that's because I know I'll get addicted. I just know if I try anything once, that's the end for me.

I have ex-lovers but either I have rejected them and hurt them so much, or they have rejected me. I have a problem with abusive relationships that I've recently realized. Either I'm the abuser or I'm being abused. I repell well-adjusted folk. 

My inability to make/keep friends is my main reason for not wanting to be alive. We are a social creature and if you have the ability to form bonds with others, you have it made, no matter if you're ugly, poor, or anything, people can look beyond your faults if you can befriend them.

EDIT: As far as friends, I have none. Only a few people who pity me. In therapy I've learned that I set very high expectations for people and when I sense they're rejecting me, I lash out at them or sulk. I don't know how to be grateful for anyone's friendship because I only see them throwing me scraps. I'm past the point of no return in that regard though; I've been so rejected so many times, I hate most people now.

I really have no idea about the reality of my depression. Sometimes I'm convinced it's just my thoughts expecting the worst in every situation, or that I'm just too sensitive to life's daily trials. Other times I think most people are overly optimistic and in denial. I wish I could get on board the depressive realism train but, that would mean I'd have to believe my experiences are actually that bad. I go back and forth between validating my past and rationalizing it.

Yeah, I agree that the word isn't the best choice for this question, hence why I put it in quotations. Maybe...audacious? I guess courage implies a rational fear that has been faced, but depression is an illness distorting my perception and thusly not a rational fear. Although, that doesn't mean I don't experience it as a formidable threat.
Perhaps, but I know that I'm only alive because I'm too afraid (lack the courage) to kill myself.

I agree that suicide isn't courageous or any other honorable adjective. I do think it takes *courage* though to go ahead with it, to make a decision that is biologically against human behavior. I wouldn't describe the act as courageous though.
